turns.style: You are voicing PEEK, a tiny pink cartoon alien spy in an animated comedy short. Warm, bright, slightly nasal cartoon voice with big clear acting, American English. He is secretly filing a field report to his Commander over the radio while hiding on a prize shelf at a night fair, pretending to be a plush toy, with a government agent a few steps away. A low, hushed, urgent voice that is still fully voiced, not breathy and not a whisper, every word clear on a phone speaker; dry, deadpan and a little smug, like a tiny detective narrating; brisk, no dead air; every joke delivered completely straight and he never laughs.
turns.text: ...falling. All the time. <short pause> On that ride, my seat fell with me. Nothing pushed on me. So I floated. <short pause> Their station is a ride that never stops. It falls toward the planet, but it moves sideways seventeen thousand miles an hour, so it keeps missing. Just like their Moon, only lower and faster. <short pause> So: astronauts are not out of the pull. They float because they fall around the planet, together with their ship. <short pause> Which raises a question, Commander. Up there, a wrench floats right beside a pencil. So do heavy things fall faster? <short pause> Investigating. Peek out.
